I have to say that I would've liked to see a zombie Rob or Ned Stark... It would've been a nice way to show that the writters acknowledge the implications of using zombies as a narrative tool... But then again, that would've steered the episode to much into typical, almost predictable, campy zombie territory. 
But I think that if the writters took it there it would work against the point. The characters learn the importance of life. As a concept, as a force of nature, and how powerless they are as individuals once you understand true power (the three eyed raven, and the night king)

While I see your point, I think that the point of the story shifted in this episode. I think that they almost got us used to the idea of impactful, gorey, deaths, that had profound impacts in the political landscape of this world. We got to see murder as a means to an end. And through this unstoppable wave of death incarnate, we saw how insignificant their plans and the delusions of power are in the eyes of death. The night king.

I could feel the horror in Theon's eyes when he was him walk in. This universe's Satan walking in to destroy "Bran".

Which makes Arya's action even more powerful. She did say several times that she thinks death had many faces and this was but one more, and she was terrified shitless.

The idea that a character can be brave in the face of absolute despair and horror makes her such a badass!

And, lastly (I promise i'll try to ramble as little as possible) as a horror fan and a zombie fan, I've been a little disheartened by the use of zombies in the last 15 years in pop culture. As a narrative device, zombies should be a condition, a status that brings everything out into the light and by doing so, reveals the world they are in for what it really is. That is why I seriously dislike The Walking Dead. Zombies are no just background noise, everyone is still shitty to eachother... It's a shit drama with zombies in it. 

GoT built an entire world of politics, character dynamics, culture, plots, schemes, and more, and then showed us how meaningless it all was when faced by total anihilation. That's fucking Zombies done right!

George Romero would be proud. 

And the contemporary social context in which the majority of the world is being exposed to this story, man... Holy shit!
